key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% versus bare SA516 boiler steel after 50 cycles at 900°C.
engineering_relevance: This coating offers a promising route to improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of SA516 boiler components.
method: Applied Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Conducted cyclic air oxidation testing for 50 cycles at 900°C.
Characterized microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Bare steel showed severe oxide spalling and cracking, while improved coating performance was attributed to protective Cr₂O₃, TiO₂, NiTiO₄, and NiO phases, reduced porosity, and increased microhardness.
watch_item: Laboratory air-oxidation results do not establish long-term durability under actual boiler combustion environments.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
